name: Hagelandse wijn
summary: Belgium's first recognised wine appellation, in the rolling hills between Leuven, Aarschot, Diest and Tienen. Vines grow on its slopes over iron-rich sandy soils.
label_note: The text names the wine "Hagelandse Wijn met gecontroleerde oorsprongsbenaming" and requires all grapes to come from the recognised zone.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: The official text names Chardonnay wines that recall Burgundy as the first of three main types.

grapes.name: Müller-Thurgau
grapes.local_note: The official text names Müller-Thurgau wines, recalling those of Luxembourg, as a third type.

appellations.name: Hagelandse wijn
appellations.note: PDO for still white, rosé and red wine.

appellations.name: Vlaamse mousserende kwaliteitswijn
appellations.note: Flemish PDO for quality sparkling wine; its zone includes all of Hageland.

appellations.name: Vlaamse landwijn
appellations.note: Flemish PGI for still wine; its zone includes all of Hageland.

name: Haspengouwse wijn
summary: Haspengouwse wijn comes from the fruit-growing south of Limburg, around Sint-Truiden, Borgloon and Tongeren. Its vineyards stand on the region's loam and marl.
label_note: May carry the traditional term "Gecontroleerde oorsprongsbenaming"; all grapes must come from the recognised zone.

appellations.name: Haspengouwse wijn
appellations.note: PDO for still white, rosé and red wine.

appellations.name: Vlaamse mousserende kwaliteitswijn
appellations.note: Flemish PDO for quality sparkling wine; its zone includes all of Haspengouw.

appellations.name: Vlaamse landwijn
appellations.note: Flemish PGI for still wine; its zone includes all of Haspengouw.

name: Heuvellandse wijn
summary: Heuvellandse wijn comes from the Heuvelland hills of West Flanders, with vineyards on the flanks of the Kemmelberg, the Monteberg and their neighbours. The soils are sandy, over iron-rich sandstone.
label_note: The text names the wine "Heuvellandse Wijn met gecontroleerde oorsprongsbenaming"; all grapes must come from the recognised zone.

appellations.name: Heuvellandse wijn
appellations.note: PDO for still white, rosé and red wine.

appellations.name: Vlaamse mousserende kwaliteitswijn
appellations.note: Flemish PDO for quality sparkling wine; its zone includes all of Heuvelland.

appellations.name: Vlaamse landwijn
appellations.note: Flemish PGI for still wine; its zone includes all of Heuvelland.

name: Côtes de Sambre et Meuse
summary: Covers the Walloon part of the Meuse basin, from the Sambre and Meuse valleys to the Ourthe, Lesse and Semois. Approved in 2004, it is for still wines; Walloon sparkling wine has its own names.
label_note: May carry the traditional term "Appellation d'origine contrôlée". Grapes must be Vitis vinifera, picked in the Meuse basin and made into wine inside the zone.

appellations.name: Côtes de Sambre et Meuse
appellations.note: PDO for still white, red and rosé wine from the Meuse basin in Wallonia.

appellations.name: Crémant de Wallonie
appellations.note: PDO covering all of Wallonia; white or rosé, second fermentation in bottle, at least nine months on lees.

appellations.name: Vin mousseux de qualité de Wallonie
appellations.note: PDO covering all of Wallonia; white or rosé, traditional method.

appellations.name: Vin de pays des jardins de Wallonie
appellations.note: PGI covering all of Wallonia, for still white, red and rosé wine.

name: Moselle Luxembourgeoise
summary: Luxembourg's one appellation follows the Moselle for about 40 km, from Schengen to Wasserbillig. It makes mostly white wines, led by Rivaner, and a large share of Crémant de Luxembourg.
label_note: Labels must show "Appellation d'origine protégée" with "Moselle Luxembourgeoise". "Coteaux de" with a section, commune or canton name, and lieu-dit names, are reserved for hand-picked wines from base yields of at most 75 hl/ha.

grapes.name: Müller-Thurgau
grapes.local_note: Sold as Rivaner; about 19% of the vineyard in 2024.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: The main red grape, about 11% of the vineyard in 2024.

appellations.name: Moselle Luxembourgeoise
appellations.note: The AOP for still white, red and rosé wine and for sparkling wine.

appellations.name: Crémant de Luxembourg
appellations.note: Traditional term within the AOP, not a separate registration; bottle-fermented white or rosé.
